terms.gloss: a ridge; in the sea, a reef just under the surface
evidence: Verg. A. 1.110: dorsum immāne marī summō
terms.comment: Vergil’s word for the reef the Italians called the Altars, a huge ridge at the surface of the sea; dorsum is an animal’s back, and so any ridge (of a hill, of a road). For a coral reef, dorsum cūraliī, a description of ours. Alexander’s men reported little trees in the deep of the Indian Ocean, branching, red at the tips, and brittle as glass (Plin. NH 13.140): the coral of a reef.

terms.gloss: hidden rocks, a reef under the water

phrases.latin: Trīs Notus abreptās in saxa latentia torquet — saxa vocant Italī mediīs quae in flūctibus Ārās — dorsum immāne marī summō
phrases.english: three ships the South Wind snatches and hurls onto hidden rocks (rocks in mid-sea that the Italians call the Altars), a huge reef at the surface of the sea

phrases.latin: in altō quāsdam arbusculās colōre būbulī cornūs rāmōsās et cacūminibus rubentēs
phrases.english: in the deep, some little trees, branching, the colour of ox-horn, and red at the tips

phrases.latin: Ad dorsum natābimus et piscēs spectābimus.
phrases.english: We’ll swim out to the reef and look at the fish.

sources: Lewis & Short: dorsum · Lewis & Short: lateo
